dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, how lucky am I to have so many kind-hearted people assisting me!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah. Just watch your step, now.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Everything I've been through is starting to pay off now... There finally is a light at the end of the tunnel!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah, I see it now! What lies before me... is a whole world of hope!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...No, what lies before you is the fountain. I hope you can start seeing clearly, or you'll end up taking a dip in it!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: ...Indeed, Monsieur Neuvillette, I'd very much appreciate hearing your thoughts on everything we just discussed, including my initial proposal, and the general direction of our potential cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Your proposals are reasonable, and quite well-thought out. Your sincerity and wish for our mutual success was evident in your words, so there's no need to be so modest.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Thank you. So, what's your decision?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If you're asking for my personal opinion... I'm willing to cooperate in full based on my own opinions and my impression of Inazuma's culture.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: However, Fontaine doesn't run simply based on the feelings of one individual. I'm sure Inazuma must be the same. Everything must be done in accordance with the regulations that are in place.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Yes, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I will submit a written proposal outlining the details of our potential cooperation to the Palais Mermonia within a week.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Then I look forward to hearing from you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Here, Yoimiya, try some Conch Madeleine.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, you ordered it, Ayaka, so you should be the first to try.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: To be honest, I ordered it for you. You're fond of desserts, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe... Well, in that case, I guess I shouldn't refuse! Let's try some together!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hehe, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: This is amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The texture is so soft! You can feel the super rich aroma of butter as soon as you take a bite, and the aftertaste is pure bliss...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Great, I'm glad you like it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I enjoyed it too. And I really like the swirly design.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I've heard that it's supposed to look like a Beryl Conch! I've never actually seen one myself, but now, I'm really curious about what it looks like!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hey, Ayaka, when you can find the time, would you like to go search for one underwater with me?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Alright, why don't we go right after this?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Great, then that's a plan! There are so many places I'd like to visit with you!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: What? Never thought that the Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol could come from the Fleuve Cendre?

choices.text: I have to say, I'm pretty shocked.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Honestly, I'm pretty shocked, too. There used to be a time when I thought I would never be able to join the Gardes.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But as long as you can distinguish yourself through your accomplishments and skills, you'll eventually be recognized for your worth.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: If you look at it another way, my life at Fleuve Cendre has actually taught me a lot of valuable skills.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Skills like... how to barter with criminals, or how to think in their shoes.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Of course, I'd appreciate it if you could keep this a secret between us.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: You mean, rising through the ranks? It was a struggle, for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Even though it's a bit late, I must thank you for investigating this case with me.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not on behalf of the Special Patrol this time — it's a personal expression of gratitude from yours truly.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Ah, you want to hear more about my father?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: To be honest, I didn't spend that much time with him. He was always busy with the Special Patrol, so he would often return home really late at night. Some nights, he didn't come home at all.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Once, he didn't come home for a long time. Maybe a whole week or so.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: When I went out to buy food, I learned that he had become a criminal, and by extension, that made me a criminal's daughter.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But we can talk about that another day.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I actually have a lot of sympathy for Veronique and Baptiste. I can understand the hatred they feel for their father...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But that doesn't mean I'll allow them to walk the path of evil, even if it might lead to another sense of justice.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Films are different from the real world. They are a form of art and represent the wishes in people's hearts.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I adore "The Two Musketeers," and I'm very happy to have had the opportunity to act the role as one.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I can't wait to catch the film when it premieres in the opera house. I'm looking forward to seeing the audience's reaction to the climactic ending.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Thank you for looking out for me. I'll see you at the award ceremony — I'd be very surprised if we don't win.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Is there something I can help you with?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Interested in our couture services? Just give me the word.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But we didn't really do anything...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: There's no need to be humble. You helped Xavier and Chevreuse, and even Kirara's told me many good things about you. They are all my friends.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Thanks to you, we were also able to premiere the film in time. Its success has increased the reach of my brand.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You've done far more than what you give yourself credit for.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I am merely a fashion designer. I don't have anything else I moonlight as.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But when you run a business, it's inevitable that as you make more friends, you'll also encounter all sorts of thorny issues.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You scratch my back, I'll scratch yours. It's just the common sense of business.

choices.text: I don't have any more questions.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Okay, see you around.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: About the film...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Xavier's over the moon now that he's actually won the Furina Award. Maybe I'll actually find him in a fountain the next time I see him.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The demand for couture at my Boutique has also increased... so much so that I don't have enough staff to handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Looks like I'm one step closer to achieving my dream.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Anyway, you will always be welcome at Chioriya Boutique. I would love to see you both again at the upcoming Fontaine Fashion Week as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'm so glad we were able to complete the film. Thanks for taking care of me while I was here.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Really? Thank you...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: At first, I simply tried to work hard out of a desire to not become a burden to the crew. It would have been so embarrassing if the filming had to stop to accommodate my lack of skills.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: But Director Furina was both patient and knowledgeable, and Chevreuse and Elain taught me a lot about the scenes and details. It was all thanks to their help that I was able to grow comfortable with the role.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: And even with all of that said, I still... got a little flustered with praise, especially since everyone, including you, were complimenting me at the end...

choices.text: Did you have a good time?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Yes, I visited many places with Yoimiya in between the filming sessions.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: The elegant streets, the beautiful flowers and greenery, and the dreamlike underwater world... Everything I saw will shine like stars in my memories.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: It also brings me joy to think that perhaps you've marveled at those exact wonders as well.

choices.text: Thank you for your hard work, Ayaka.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Ah, it's nothing at all. I... don't often have the opportunity to wander out into the world like this.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Not only did I make many new friends during this trip, I also picked up many new skills from everyone around me. I will cherish this experience greatly.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Oh, and I'm also going to bring some Conch Madeleines back to the Yashiro Commission as a gift.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: If we could enjoy them with some coffee... Hehe, perhaps it'll feel as if I'd never left Fontaine at all.

choices.text: Have a safe and relaxing trip home.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Mhm, thank you for looking out for me. Please do take care of yourself during your adventures as well.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: If the stars align, we'll see each other in Inazuma again.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Lady Furina, please allow me to take just one more photo of you! I would also love to get your autograph... just as a memento of our time together on the crew.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey, I've had enough of the Kamera flashes from when we were all up on stage.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: But... But Lady Furina, you are the best Director I've ever met! The most photogenic maiden in all of Fontaine! This kind of lively and celebratory setting is exactly where you shine. I believe all photographers would agree...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Come, the brightest star of our land! Show us your light! The Kamera is waiting to sing praises of your beauty!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well I'm flattered, but... but...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, I'll humor you and try a few more different poses.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But I don't have to hold the trophy, right?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah... Ah! Of course! You may pose however you like!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, thank you so much! By the heavens, my luck has been beyond belief, I'm having a hard time coming to terms with it now...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Miss Yoimiya... We haven't had the chance to talk, but please accept my thanks for everything you've done over the past few days.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh? But I feel like I didn't do anything out of the ordinary.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'm very grateful for your assistance during that special performance in the warehouse.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It was always going to be somewhat risky. To engage and draw away Morris all on your own...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You're only a civilian and have never been trained to act in such a dangerous situation...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't say it like that! As the director's assistant, it was my duty to help out the crew however I could. It was an honor to help you solve the case.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I have to admit though, my heart was thumping super hard the entire time I was laying on the ground. I was scared that everyone would notice, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You did great.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, and before I forget! If you ever visit Inazuma, please come and pay a visit to Naganohara Fireworks. I'll make some fireworks for you — I even know what shape I'd make!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'm guessing... a musket?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, telling you now would ruin the surprise! If you really want to see it, just come and visit me!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Oh, I didn't expect to meet you here.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I've been told that this is a beverage called "Fonta." I quite like its unique taste.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The slogan, "A Font of Refreshment," is rather catchy as well. I'm starting to wonder if I could incorporate it into our cultural exchange initiative.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: What would happen if we were to add some sprigs of mint into Fonta? I believe this is an idea worth testing.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Or perhaps we could even take it one step further, and mix in an equal amount of Milk Tea Medley...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hehe, but for some reason, I suspect that experiment wouldn't turn out well.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Thanks to you, the film was successfully completed and the Yashiro Commission secured a collaboration project with the Palais Mermonia.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If another opportunity was to arise in the future, perhaps I should take on the chance to act as the protagonist.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Or perhaps... you think the role of villain would fit me better?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Thank you for the well wishes. I will take good care of Ayaka and Yoimiya.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I would like to wish you safe travels on your next journey as well.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: How about it? Ready to try your hand at filming?

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Excellent. I've already set up the scene, the actors are ready, and all is awaiting your arrival.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Lumiere is much older than I, but that poses no obstacle to us brothers working together.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: We were not yet famous when we filmed "The Arrival of an Aquabus" and "Employees Leaving the Factory."

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: We two brothers have done everything together, because no one was willing to assist directors who were not yet famous, haha!

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: If you are interested, you can go see those two films.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: No problem, I understand. A quality product requires time to incubate and nurture.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: Super Zenith Boss-Level Force, do you have any further instructions?

choices.text: Let's play a round of "Thousand-Pace Interdiction Arcminute Sharpshooting Zone"!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: No problem! This game doesn't use up any real ammunition, and the targets don't require maintenance, so you can play as many rounds as you like!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Oh, interested in a custom-made musket of your own?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Though I couldn't tell you exactly how muskets work myself, I do recall hearing colleagues mention the names of several outstanding gunsmiths.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: In terms of their lifespan, accuracy, and ballistic stability, there's simply no comparison between a mass-produced musket and one that has been painstakingly crafted by a gunsmith...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: And if you're using high-quality ammunition, produced to very tight tolerance levels, then get ready for some jaw-dropping results!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: But I seem to remember that regular citizens aren't allowed to carry muskets, at least not without having first cut through an absolute sea of red tape...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Tell you what, when I return to the Special Patrol headquarters, I'll ask around for you!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Nice to meet you again, Super Zenith Boss-Level Force! I'll be here waiting for you, drop by whenever you'd like!

dialogues.speaker: Helene
dialogues.text: Even though they promised to help with the testing, I still feel a little on edge...

dialogues.speaker: Helene
dialogues.text: This restless feeling... Just as I thought, getting over my client-phobia won't be as simple as that!

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Ah! You're back! I—I'm so sorry, I must have zoned out...

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: I've been thinking, is there really no way for me to escape the shadow of my clients?

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Could it be that the only solution is, as you implied, to come up with a way of "getting rid" of my boss?

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: I—I need to think this over!

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Huh? You, the miracle worker... You're interested in mechanical principles?

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Actually, there isn't anything novel about the technology itself. I just happened to make some technical breakthroughs based on some previously abandoned research...

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: I've heard that there was a bunch of very talented engineers way back when... who wanted to make cannons that could fire stably even amidst towering waves.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: To that end, they worked day and night to invent a device that could stabilize weaponry on a vertical axis.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Such projects were ultimately abandoned, sure, but I was able to restore the stabilizers based on some fragmentary documents.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: After scaling it down, the end result was the current "Stabilization Mek."

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: I wonder whether there's really a market for this type of machine...

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Oh no, what am I going to do...

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: Well, how was it? My experimental style and "Special Lighting" are quite something, no?

choices.text: I was just getting into it!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Ha, I knew you were up to the job!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Filming action scenes clearly suits you like a suit.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Feel free to drop by the studio anytime during the Film Festival to carry on filming, and immerse yourself in the limelight!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: I literally have an inexhaustible supply of film roll, so no matter how many cuts you want to film, be my guest!

choices.text: When will the film come out?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Hard to say, to be honest...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Even after you and your acting double have finished all the filming, I've then got to go through the whole process of editing, color grading, sound design, and more...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: I'm not even sure if it'll all be done in time to start officially promoting it and put out a trailer.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: But none of our work will have been wasted! Even if it all takes a day or two extra, when the film finally comes out, its quality will speak for itself!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: So please, have patience, my good partner.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Goodbye for now. Remember, when you get some time on your hands, please do pop into the studio for a bit of filming!
